grammar.change_scope: withdrew library operator export (OPART-001/002/003), narrowed OPLIB-003 to the local operator source area, revised OPBOOT-003 to a single-pass import-independent bootstrap, and added the OPDECL family with a separate operator-source grammar rooted at operator-source-file

structural_checks.decision_sync_policy: Executable grammar decisions must occur in both the EBNF and register. Configuration, bootstrap-order, artifact-projection, ownership, conflict, conformance-profile, and withdrawn historical decisions may be reference/register-only when they do not change an executable production.

secondary_roots.reason: DECISION-OPDECL-004: the operator source area is parsed by a separate grammar before ordinary source; deliberately not reachable from compilation-unit

design_assertions.description: Local functions require a block definition and cannot be forward declarations.
Anonymous function, lambda, anonymous class and block forms are expressions.
Anonymous class expressions carry no declaration name.
forall is reachable through type-expression.
Ordinary function-declaration is not a direct package primary.
The grammar records declaration-site lexical scope for ordinary local functions.
The grammar records @co.dap.inner call-site lexical-context resolution.
Object construction is an expression and does not use body-close.
Pattern block bodies and expression results keep separate termination.
Direct anonymous function bindings use body termination.
Named UDT bodies use body-close.
Built-in directives are self-delimiting.
Enum variants are comma-separated.
Identifier production enforces ASCII-leading identifier shape.
Numeric literal productions do not admit apostrophe/underscore digit separators.
Boolean and none literals use co.const spellings.
Dependent indices use the dedicated index production; dependentType is a direct type kind, and a function-shaped type constructor has exactly one type-producing result (possibly one union).

evidence.type-constructor-primary:
annotations, function-name, parameter-list,
                           { parameter-list }, type-constructor-return-clause,
                           type-constructor-binding

design_assertions.description: Planned grammar constructs remain represented.
~, # and ^ are reserved prefix spellings and @ is excluded from prefix-operator.

Existing-operator overload is supported only in extension units, struct companion units, or class methods; normalized receiver/implicit-this operands obey owner and language-owned arity rules; override and extends modes are unsupported.
fol-conf.yaml configures operator_library_folder.
Configured operators.fol is parsed with core syntax and produces no independent artifact.
Ordinary library artifacts embed operator tables beside symbol tables.
Normal direct library imports load symbol and operator tables together without a special import placement; transitive operators are not activated.
Duplicate custom symbols and built-in/reserved/future glyph claims are rejected without merge or overload.
Exported operator metadata includes complete parse/link schema.
Local operator source and normal direct-library metadata are conflict-checked before operator-dependent source parsing.
Alpha custom operators are restricted to infix, prefix, and postfix.
The operator source grammar is rooted at operator-source-file and is not reachable from compilation-unit, so ordinary source parsing cannot enter it.
library-member admits no production able to carry an operator implementation, so operators cannot appear in a library surface file.

notes: Revision 19 changes entry-type-declaration and member-suffix from folang-r18.ebnf; production and reachability counts are unchanged.
co.lang.dependentType, co.lang.typetype, and co.lang.typekind use type-first declaration routing and are excluded from general-declarable-kind.
Function-shaped type constructors reject zero, named, comma-separated, and multiple returns; one union of type-producing kinds remains one return.

Supported named unit, module, object, instance, matcher, block, delegate, function-object, and data declarations retain complete generic parameter clauses; application-entry declarations, libraries, and package aliases do not accept them.
Record patterns, grouped variable declarations, expression tuples, and function-type heads require another item after each comma and reject a trailing comma.

Contextual lambda and wildcard arguments require receiver-qualified collection member calls, transparent grouping preserves that context, and wildcard is accepted only as each argument zero; contains, containsVal, and each's value argument require actual values.
The hard-reserved comprehension keyword for is also admitted contextually by member-suffix for the documented .for built-in method.

Existing-operator mode=overload is supported only through a built-in extension function inside a unit, a struct companion-unit function, or a class operator method; normalized owner operands obey language-owned arity, omitted mode defaults only for existing overloads, and override/extends are unsupported.
Project-local new operators use mode=define in <operator_library_folder>/operators.fol. Reserved future mathematical/modifier glyphs cannot be claimed.
Normal direct library imports load projected symbol and exported operator tables from the same .folib/.folenc artifact; no special operator import placement is introduced.
